mathematical_justification.clause: Exact distinguished leaf and side separation
mathematical_justification.assessment: The contractedLeaf endpoints are the consecutive positions lower and lower+1. Negating containment of both endpoints in a strict interval J implies J.right<=lower or lower+1<=J.left by integer order. Thus an interval excluding the formal leaf lies entirely to one side, and touching an endpoint is allowed. The independent consumer proves the converse as well, and the two inverse consumers explicitly allow touching either endpoint. This matches the source other-child disjoint-interior condition; it does not incorrectly demand disjoint closed endpoints or assume that a general positive-length old interval can only overlap wholly.

mathematical_justification.clause: Exact leaf count and unit-array transport
mathematical_justification.assessment: On the left side expandPosition is the identity on both endpoints. On the right it adds the same erasedInteriorCount to both. Subtracting those actual endpoint values preserves J.leaves exactly. The strict endpoint inequalities ensure the natural-number subtraction characterizes right=left+1 without truncation ambiguity. Therefore the source unit array, one on a single leaf and zero otherwise, is transported exactly. The independent leaf consumer checks both actual inverse values equal one when J has one leaf. No zero nonleaf right-hand side is substituted on a unary interval.
